developmentObservations.interpretation: Four retained formal attempts have exact seven-source snapshots and argv/Node/log/result/aware-time bindings. Initial selected ten cases pass before the filesystem-allocation case was added; initial full runtime has four old-contract assertion failures, retained verbatim. Revised full runtime passes after those witnesses are updated. A concrete first-winner review fix then preserves a previously selected cancellation/timeout over a later progress-provider rejection, followed by the final full-runtime pass. The first three attempts have historical runtime/test bytes and are not final-source coverage; only the fourth matches final source. currentSourceUnchanged is within each attempt, not equality with the final source. No separate development orchestration program is archived and no completeness of all discovery/development/tool history is claimed

limits: Foreground cancellation and SDK deadline may return command false and close progress before the real workflow settles. The source gate, drain and owned output remain held until actual settlement; repeat same-file commands return false without competing builds, while other files remain independent.

Late workflow failures remain observed. Dispatched selected-project delegation retains its prior actual-settlement policy because exact session ownership is unavailable. A foreground cancellation at the owned file-app handoff gap targets only the exact launch matched to generated output; pending-start ownership remains conservative. Generic runProcess behavior is unchanged, and foreground settlement does not establish provider termination or cleanup completion. A provider that never settles may retain the source gate and shutdown drain indefinitely.
The one installed ordinary HTTP control is normal-flow regression only, without native cancellation, held-provider or SDK-deadline injection.
Full issue18 AC6 and issue45's earlier unexplained B pause/failed compiler observation remain open; no hard OS request or whole-phase deadline is implied.
No physical F5/menu, macOS, calibrated total-phase budget, descendant cleanup, language-service readiness, CI, release or publication qualification is claimed.
